profileContract.supportedMeans: A released adapter has a selected mechanism, declared fidelity, explicit missing surfaces, a per-client executable-resolution proof when executable access is claimed, and qualification evidence.
profileContract.releaseInvariant: The same installed Legion release, capability identifiers, tool schemas, semantic results, and release-binding handshake apply to every executable client integration.
hostResponsibilities: trust, permission, authentication, and sandbox prompts
MCP process start, cancellation, restart, and shutdown

requires: measured qualification for every claimed runtime and host surface
prohibits: claiming Full from Agent Plugins conformance alone
claiming Full before executable-resolution proof passes

requires: an explicit list of every missing surface
safe behavior despite each missing surface
prohibits: claiming an unavailable enforcement or executable surface

requires: a specific installation or safe-operation failure

targetMechanismOrder: minimal client-native bridge only when required
referenceClients.releaseFidelity: Full only after setup verifies skills, a reusable client-owned stdio MCP process, release binding, bare-command resolution or a supported exact-path registration, and every claimed enforcement surface.
degradedWhen: the selected mechanism exposes only a safe subset
bare command lookup fails and no supported exact-path registration exists
a claimed enforcement surface is not measured

targetMechanismOrder: minimal client-native bridge only when required

officialPiPath.mechanism: versioned, release-bound instructions and skills only; no executable Legion registration
officialPiPath.selectionRule: This is Pi's only M0-approved release path because the authorized current source explicitly marks its native-agent and MCP mechanisms unconfirmed.

the Pi integration has no executable Legion workflow
officialPiPath.promotionRule: Pi may move to Degraded or Full only after a supported Pi mechanism, path ownership, executable-resolution proof, release-binding handshake, and lifecycle qualification are recorded. A Pi-native bridge may be introduced only when that verified mechanism requires it and remains mechanical.
